question: Should OpenClaw accept the RFC’s grouped Claw lifecycle and this `claws update --dry-run` command plus `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` schema as a core experimental contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent but adds a new cross-owner core product surface absent from current main, and the RFC and dependent stack slices remain draft without human approval.

options.title: Approve the ordered RFC stack
options.body: Resolve the RFC questions, review the preceding ownership slices, and land this planner before the consented apply PR.

options.title: Narrow the lifecycle contract
options.body: Reduce the owner scope or public CLI/schema before any dependent update behavior lands.

options.title: Pause the Claws feature
options.body: Keep or close the draft stack without merge if this lifecycle does not fit core product direction.

recommendation.title: Approve the ordered RFC stack
recommendation.body: Resolve the RFC questions, review the preceding ownership slices, and land this planner before the consented apply PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest adjacent core CLI/state history candidate and the decision is repository-level product direction.
